_readme: THE BORE AT THE MOUTH (2026-10-26, Mark: "a rolling wave on the coast"). A 500 m impactor 800 km off the Merrimack (40.5 N 63 W;
a 1 km one there swung the sea side -110 to +130 m and swallowed the eye; Ward & Asphaug's 1950 DA stood at 35 N 70 W), the eye
80 m over the north jetty's tip looking out to sea, from 16:02Z through the arrival at 30x: the sea drains off the bar, then the
surge comes over it into the standing water of the inlet as a BORE, and the bank kernel feeds its face to the crest law (the cusp,
the roller, the flight where the bed is steep), the column plane folds where the labels overtake, its whitewater Belanger's.
The mid-Atlantic 1 km event's rise here was minutes long and showed no face; the bore wants a front that is steep at the shore.
